newsitem.title: USA: Beef movement seen key to US Plains cattle outlook.
newsitem.headline: Beef movement seen key to US Plains cattle outlook.

text.p: Trade was very slow in Plains feedlot cattle on Wednesday with showlists almost sold out after heavy volume on Tuesday, feeedlot sources said.

They noted sales in Texas this week have totalled about 111,000 head so far, slightly above the showlist of around 104,000 while Kansas sales as of late afternoon Wednesday stood at around 85,000 versus a showlist of about 95,000 head.

The bulk of trade has been at $66 per cwt, up $2 from most trade last week with the potential for further gains seen dependent on whether boxed beef can be moved at the highest prices since December 1996.
"Beef has made a good move but I'm hearing some retailers are starting to back off. They've got the price where it is not competitive with pork and poultry right now," a Texas feedlot source said.
USDA boxed beef cut-out values for heavyweight choice were at the highest levels since December 1996 on Wednesday after rising $0.60 per cwt to $108.78.
"If he (the packer) starts to stack up boxes or cut his margins to move it then I figure his next move is going to be to cut back on what he is paying for the product coming in," the source said.
